findings.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:105 — Updating `tu.notification_level` with `tu.save!` bypasses `TopicUser.change`, so an email unsubscribe neither emits the `/topic/:id` notification-level event nor records the standard user-change metadata, leaving already-open clients stale and this override outside the model’s notification-state contract.

spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb:179 — `expect(message_with_unsubscribe.body).to match(builder.template_args[:user_preferences_url])` verifies only the pre-existing account-preferences URL, so the new per-topic `unsubscribe_url` can be omitted or fail to render while the feature's only added unsubscribe test still passes.

config/routes.rb:440 — P1 (confidence 99%, anchor: the state-changing route is verbatim `get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"`) Any cross-origin page can request this GET while a victim is signed in, silently changing that victim's topic notification level because GET bypasses Rails CSRF protection.

P1 app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:107 — `if tu.notification_level > TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular]` makes the emailed GET a toggle, so a retry, link prefetch, or second click after a successful unsubscribe silently changes the user from muted back to regular and resumes topic email delivery.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/topic-from-params.js.es6:5 — P3: The unrelated topic-navigation refactor `model(params) { return params; }` expands a per-topic email-unsubscribe change into the core topic route, so a regression or rollback of this feature now requires separately reviewing/reverting navigation code; even if intended as no-op cleanup, it has no dependency on the unsubscribe path and therefore remains scope drift.

app/models/topic_user.rb:64 — P3: The unrelated model cleanup `topic_users.each { |ftu| result[ftu.topic_id] = ftu }` changes shared topic-user lookup code despite the feature using only the unsubscribe controller's direct query, so any lookup regression or feature rollback carries unrelated notification-model churn; although it may be behavior-preserving style cleanup, it is not required to deliver per-topic email unsubscribe and remains scope drift.

app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:105 — P2: The GET /t/:topic_id/unsubscribe action mutates the authenticated user's notification level without a CSRF token or origin check, so an attacker can force a logged-in victim to load a chosen topic URL and silently mute or downgrade that topic's notifications.

spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb:179 — The added test passes `unsubscribe_url` but asserts only the default preferences URL, so it remains green if the new `%{unsubscribe_url}` interpolation is omitted or broken and notification emails contain no usable per-topic unsubscribe link.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:105 — Updating `tu.notification_level` with `tu.save!` bypasses `TopicUser.change`, so an email unsubscribe neither emits the `/topic/:id` notification-level event nor records the standard user-change metadata, leaving already-open clients stale and this override outside the model’s notification-state contract.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the new `unsubscribe` action in topics_controller.rb (lines 98-117) directly modifies `tu.notification_level` and calls `tu.save!` instead of using `TopicUser.change`. Looking at the diff for topic_user.rb, the `change` method includes `MessageBus.publish("/topic/#{topic_id}", { notification_level_change: attrs[:notification_level] }, user_ids: [user_id])` when notification_level changes. By bypassing this method, the unsubscribe action won't emit the MessageBus event that notifies open clients of the notification level change, leaving them with stale state. This is a real behavioral inconsistency/bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb:179 — `expect(message_with_unsubscribe.body).to match(builder.template_args[:user_preferences_url])` verifies only the pre-existing account-preferences URL, so the new per-topic `unsubscribe_url` can be omitted or fail to render while the feature's only added unsubscribe test still passes.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the test at line 179 only checks for user_preferences_url in the body, not the new unsubscribe_url that was added. Looking at the diff, the test adds unsubscribe_url to the message builder options (line 171), but the existing assertion only verifies the pre-existing URL. The new per-topic unsubscribe functionality (added in config/locales/server.en.yml showing the unsubscribe_link template now includes both URLs) should have test coverage to verify the unsubscribe_url is actually rendered in the output. This is a legitimate missing test concern for newly added functionality.

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/routes.rb:440 — P1 (confidence 99%, anchor: the state-changing route is verbatim `get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"`) Any cross-origin page can request this GET while a victim is signed in, silently changing that victim's topic notification level because GET bypasses Rails CSRF protection.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a new GET route at line 440: `get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"`. The `unsubscribe` action in topics_controller.rb modifies the user's TopicUser notification_level (lines 103-112) and saves it. Since this is a GET request, Rails CSRF protection does not apply, meaning any cross-origin page can trigger this state-changing action when a victim is logged in. This is a real security vulnerability - GET requests should not perform state-changing operations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1 app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:107 — `if tu.notification_level > TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular]` makes the emailed GET a toggle, so a retry, link prefetch, or second click after a successful unsubscribe silently changes the user from muted back to regular and resumes topic email delivery.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a real bug in the unsubscribe action. Looking at lines 107-112 in topics_controller.rb, the logic is: if notification_level > regular, set to regular; else set to muted. This means: (1) First click when watching/tracking: level becomes regular. (2) Second click (retry/prefetch): since level is now regular (not > regular), it becomes muted. (3) Third click: since level is muted (not > regular), it stays muted. However, the finding says it toggles 'from muted back to regular', which is incorrect - once muted, it stays muted. But the core issue is valid: the GET request is not idempotent. A user who was 'watching' expects to unsubscribe, but a retry/prefetch could change behavior unexpectedly. The first request sets to 'regular' (still receiving some notifications), and only subsequent requests set to 'muted'. This is a real bug where link prefetching or retries cause inconsistent behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/topic-from-params.js.es6:5 — P3: The unrelated topic-navigation refactor `model(params) { return params; }` expands a per-topic email-unsubscribe change into the core topic route, so a regression or rollback of this feature now requires separately reviewing/reverting navigation code; even if intended as no-op cleanup, it has no dependency on the unsubscribe path and therefore remains scope drift.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims that changes to topic-from-params.js.es6 are 'unrelated' scope drift. However, looking at the diff, the changes in that file are purely syntactic modernization (var->const, function syntax updates, whitespace) with no behavioral changes. These are standard code cleanup changes that often accompany feature work. The claim that this creates rollback complexity is speculative - the changes are trivial refactoring that don't affect functionality. This is a style/process opinion rather than a concrete code issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_user.rb:64 — P3: The unrelated model cleanup `topic_users.each { |ftu| result[ftu.topic_id] = ftu }` changes shared topic-user lookup code despite the feature using only the unsubscribe controller's direct query, so any lookup regression or feature rollback carries unrelated notification-model churn; although it may be behavior-preserving style cleanup, it is not required to deliver per-topic email unsubscribe and remains scope drift.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims this is 'scope drift' and 'unrelated model cleanup' that could cause issues. However, looking at the diff, the change from a multi-line each block to a single-line `topic_users.each { |ftu| result[ftu.topic_id] = ftu }` is purely a style/formatting change that is behavior-preserving. The finding itself acknowledges it 'may be behavior-preserving style cleanup'. This is a pure style/format nit - the code does exactly the same thing before and after. There's no actual defect or important issue here, just a stylistic preference about whether cleanup should be bundled with feature work.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:105 — P2: The GET /t/:topic_id/unsubscribe action mutates the authenticated user's notification level without a CSRF token or origin check, so an attacker can force a logged-in victim to load a chosen topic URL and silently mute or downgrade that topic's notifications.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a new `unsubscribe` action in topics_controller.rb that modifies the user's notification level (tu.notification_level = ...; tu.save!) via a GET request. The action is added to skip_before_filter :check_xhr and requires authentication (not in skip_before_filter :ensure_logged_in). GET requests don't have CSRF protection in Rails by default, and the route is defined as a GET route in routes.rb. This means an attacker could craft a link that, when clicked by a logged-in user, would silently change their notification settings for a topic. This is a legitimate CSRF vulnerability.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb:179 — The added test passes `unsubscribe_url` but asserts only the default preferences URL, so it remains green if the new `%{unsubscribe_url}` interpolation is omitted or broken and notification emails contain no usable per-topic unsubscribe link.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the test at line 179 adds `unsubscribe_url: "/t/1234/unsubscribe"` to the test parameters but only asserts that 'List-Unsubscribe header' is present (line 175-176). Looking at the diff, the test doesn't verify that the new `%{unsubscribe_url}` interpolation in the email template (added in server.en.yml) actually works correctly. The test would pass even if the unsubscribe_url was never interpolated into the email body. This is a legitimate test coverage gap for newly added functionality - the per-topic unsubscribe link feature is added but not properly tested.
